narrative.overview:
EquiFreight is an operations desk read after dark: a deep navy canvas, cards one step lighter, hairline borders, and a single gold fitting that marks the one thing to do next. Everything else is information, and information is either a name (set in Fraunces, a warm serif that gives places and horses their dignity), prose (Outfit, plain and even), or data (DM Mono, for the values you would copy into a form). The system never decorates; its only material flourish is the brass stall nameplate on a horse's coat colour, which replaces photography.

Density is moderate and table-like. Pages are 1440 wide with a 1200 content column (120 px gutters). Surfaces are flat, bordered panels at 12 px radius, stacked with 24 to 32 px gaps; depth comes from tonal steps between canvas, sunken wells and cards, not from shadow. Status is always said twice, as a tone and as a word, and every deadline is said twice, as time left and as a date. The newest surface (customer request tracking) is the reference for how pages open: the route or page name as a Fraunces title, the code and summary beneath it in mono and prose, status chips top right, then what the reader owes.

Dark is the primary mode. Light is a second mode of the same `EquiFreight / Color` variable collection, applied per frame; its values live in `.impeccable/design.json` (`colorMeta.<token>.light`). Desktop 1440 is the maintained scope. Mobile frames (the mobile app header and "My horses · Mobile" in both modes) exist in the file but are not maintained; do not treat them as reference.
keyCharacteristics: Navy canvas (#0C1520) with card, raised and muted surfaces stepping up in lightness.
One filled-gold button per view; gold never carries status.
Status in four tones (ok, warn, bad, info) plus neutral, always with a word.
Three type voices with fixed jobs: Fraunces for names and headings, Outfit for prose and labels, DM Mono for data.
Deadlines shown twice; estimates shown as ranges; demo figures marked as demo.
Flat bordered panels, 12 px corners, hairline dividers; shadow only for overlays, focus and brass.
24 px line icons, 1.75 stroke, round caps.

rules.name: The One Gold Button Rule
rules.body: A view has at most one filled gold button, and it is the action that moves the job forward. In a list of owed items only the top item's action is gold; the rest are Secondary. Gold tints (accent-text, accent-soft, accent-line) may mark selection, focus, the active nav item and the brand, but never state.

rules.name: The Gold Is Not a Status Rule
rules.body: Nothing that describes the state of a document, stage, horse or job is gold. State uses ok, warn, bad, info or neutral.

rules.name: The Said-Twice Rule
rules.body: Status is a tone plus a word ("Departure locked", "Cleared", "Waiting for you"); a coloured dot or border alone never carries meaning.

rules.name: The Three Voices Rule
rules.body: Fraunces for places, horse names and headings. Outfit for prose, people's names and labels. DM Mono for codes, dates, times, counts and distances. The two small uppercase mono styles (Mono Label, Mono Chip) are the only mono text that carries words, and only as tags on data. A value row puts a name in Label S and a code or distance in Mono Data (Vehicle "Trailer TX-447" mono; Driver "Minh" Outfit).

rules.name: The Two-Line Deadline Rule
rules.body: Every deadline is shown twice: time left first (Label S, toned by urgency: "Overdue by 1 day", "Due in 4 days"), then the date beneath it (Mono Caption, text-tertiary: "30 Sep 2026"), right-aligned.

rules.name: The Flat Panel Rule
rules.body: Panels, rows and cards carry a 1 px border and no shadow. If something needs to stand out, give it a surface step or a tone, not a drop shadow.

dos: **Do** give each view exactly one Brass Gold (#C9AA5A) filled button, on the action that moves the job forward; make every other action Secondary or Ghost.
**Do** state every status as a tone plus a word, using the ok, warn, bad, info or neutral chip.
**Do** show every deadline as time left (Label S, toned) over the date (Mono Caption, tertiary).
**Do** set places, routes and horse names in Fraunces, people and prose in Outfit, and codes, dates, times, counts and distances in DM Mono.
**Do** show customer estimates as a range ("$11,300 – $16,100") with a line saying it is not a quote.
**Do** open a page with its subject as the Fraunces title, the code and summary beneath, and status chips top right.
**Do** name the rule, the value found and the fix in every error or refusal, and keep refused actions visible but disabled.
**Do** mark demo figures as demo (the footer reads "Prototype · demo data as of ...").

**Do** fill a numbers band with commitments the system enforces (6 countries, 21-day cross-border lead time, 7-day quotation validity, one groom per 3 horses), not operating results the product cannot yet claim.
donts: **Don't** use gold for any state, progress tone or status chip.

**Don't** put an eyebrow label (small uppercase text above a heading) anywhere; the page or section title stands alone, with its summary beneath. The old role-dot Eyebrow component has been removed from the library.
**Don't** set names, places or sentences in DM Mono, or codes and dates in Fraunces or Outfit.
**Don't** show a single price before a quotation exists.
**Don't** present placeholder statistics ("4,200+ horses moved", "99.2% on-time") as real operating figures.
**Don't** use colour alone for meaning: no bare dots, borders or bars without a word beside them.
**Don't** add drop shadows to panels or cards; use a surface step or a border.
**Don't** draw live map tiles, moving dots or times finer than the recorded checkpoints on route views.
**Don't** use stock photography for horses; use the nameplate on the coat colour.
